The Interaction API is how a sign-in page reaches the QAuth engine ([ADR-019](/reference/records/adr/019-deployment-topology-and-trust-boundaries/), Decision 6). The reference ceremony app, and any UI that replaces it, reads the current step of an interaction, answers it and follows the result, until the interaction ends in a redirect. It shares its step grammar with the FiPA authorization challenge endpoint, the transport for first-party native apps ([ADR-017](/reference/records/adr/017-first-party-login/), Decision 3): a step is the same object on both, and only the envelope differs.

Status: this is the contract, published before the implementation. The auth server serves the document today; the operations it describes arrive with the Interaction API implementation.

The contract is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, [openapi.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json), and one JSON Schema per step, under `/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/`. The auth server serves the same document at `/interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json`. The typed client in `libs/shared/interaction-client` is generated from it. Both are generated from `libs/shared/interaction-contract`, and the stable-surface check compares them with the last release ([ADR-018](/reference/records/adr/018-1-0-scope-and-stability/) §5).

## Rules

- Browser-facing and same-origin. A page calls the API on the realm origin it was served from. A flow cookie (`__Host-qauth_flow`) and a CSRF value protect it, and the server sends no CORS headers.
- Typed data from the auth server’s own records, never HTML. Every string a response carries is an enum, a constant or a bounded value with a pattern. A display value has no markup bracket, no control, format, private-use or unassigned character, no line separator, and no space at either end.
- No URL carries `return_to`, a redirect or a client parameter. A page reads one opaque interaction id from its own URL, and the client, the redirect target and everything else it shows come from the API.
- The interaction id alone reads the current step, with no personal data. Personal data, such as the account chooser’s list, needs the flow cookie and a same-origin request. Answering a step or cancelling the interaction needs the flow cookie, the step’s CSRF value and a same-origin request.
- Every operation answers with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## Versioning

- The path carries the major version. Until QAuth 1.0.0 it is a release candidate, `/interaction/v1-rc.<M>` (today `/interaction/v1-rc.0`), and nothing about it is promised: a breaking change raises `<M>`. The release that ships 1.0.0 serves `/interaction/v1`.
- Within a major version, changes are additive only: new operations, new steps, new optional request members, new response members, and new values of an extensible set (step names, problem codes, fonts).
- A client ignores response members it does not know, and a page shows its error page for a step it does not know. A request with a member the operation does not declare is refused.
- The published schemas close response objects (`additionalProperties: false`) to describe this version exactly. A later version may add members, so a client must not validate responses strictly against an older schema, and ignores the members it does not know.
- Removing or renaming a member, changing a type, tightening validation, changing a status code, removing an operation or a step, and adding to a closed set, such as a step’s errors, need a new major version.
- A successor major version is served beside the previous one for at least 12 months, and the previous one stays until the next major release of QAuth.
- A step is named `urn:qauth:ia:<name>:v1-rc.<M>` until 1.0.0 and `urn:qauth:ia:<name>:v1` from then on, with the same release candidate as the path. QAuth never renames a step; if a registry of standard step names appears, its names are added beside QAuth’s.

## Operations

Every operation sits under `/interaction/v1-rc.0`. The flow cookie is `__Host-qauth_flow`. An operation's success and error responses are listed in the document, each error with the codes it may carry.

| Operation                                  | Request                                             | Flow cookie | CSRF value | Success  | Errors                                      |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Read the current step                      | `GET /interaction/v1-rc.0/{interactionId}`          | No          | No         | 200      | 410, 421, 429, 500, 503                     |
| Read the personal data of the current step | `GET /interaction/v1-rc.0/{interactionId}/personal` | Yes         | No         | 200      | 403, 410, 421, 429, 500, 503                |
| Answer the current step                    | `POST /interaction/v1-rc.0/{interactionId}/answer`  | Yes         | Yes        | 200, 303 | 400, 403, 410, 413, 415, 421, 429, 500, 503 |
| Cancel the interaction                     | `POST /interaction/v1-rc.0/{interactionId}/cancel`  | Yes         | Yes        | 200, 303 | 400, 403, 410, 413, 415, 421, 429, 500, 503 |

An answer is `application/json` or a plain HTML form post (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) with the same members, so the password, email-code and TOTP steps work without JavaScript. A JSON answer gets one of two results:

- **Next step** (`"result": "step"`): the interaction as a step read now returns it. A refused answer, such as a wrong password, gets the same step back with its `error` set and a new CSRF value. An answer after which the sign-in starts again at its first step, because the engine ended its transaction, gets that first step with a `notice` saying why: `code_burned`, `subject_mismatch`, `expired`.
- **Final redirect** (`"result": "redirect"`): the `location` the browser goes to, taken from the interaction record and the realm, never from the request.

A form post gets the same as a `303 See Other`. Anything the API refuses is an **error**: a problem document (below).

A `notice` is carried once: by the result of the JSON answer, or, after a form post, by the next step read; every later read carries none. It names no account, and before a factor succeeded it is the same for every identifier (ADR-017 Decision 4). An upstream provider's callback that refuses while the interaction is live, and a refused upstream link, come back the same way, as the `upstream` and `upstream_link` steps' `error` (#1081, #1106): the auth server shows no page of its own for them. A step read with an `error` carries the `trace_id` of the request that refused the step, which may be that callback rather than an answer, so a page shows it as it shows a problem document's.

## Steps

Each step is named `urn:qauth:ia:<name>:v1-rc.0`. A step read names the current step (`step`), the other steps the engine accepts next (`alternatives`), their params keyed by step name (`params`) and, after a refused answer, the reason (`error`): the shape of the FiPA endpoint's answer, so a new step is a new name and a new member, not a break. A step's params are what any reader of the interaction id may see; its personal data needs the flow cookie. Each step's schema file holds the whole step as one record (params, answer, personal data, errors and `amr`) with its example, which the implementation reuses as a test vector. The params and answer fields keep the step grammar's names on both transports, which is why they are `snake_case` while the envelope is `camelCase`.

| Step                                  | Transports      | Answer fields            | Errors                                                                                                                        | `amr`        | Personal data                              |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| [`identifier`](#identifier)           | Both            | `login_hint`             | —                                                                                                                             | —            | `login_hint`                               |
| [`password`](#password)               | Both            | `password`, `login_hint` | `invalid_credentials`                                                                                                         | `pwd`        | `identifier`                               |
| [`email_code`](#email_code)           | Both            | `otp`                    | `invalid_credentials`, `code_expired`                                                                                         | —            | `identifier`                               |
| [`new_password`](#new_password)       | Both            | `new_password`           | `password_rejected`                                                                                                           | —            | `identifier`                               |
| [`password_reset`](#password_reset)   | Both            | `login_hint`             | —                                                                                                                             | —            | —                                          |
| [`captcha`](#captcha)                 | Both            | `captcha_token`          | `captcha_failed`                                                                                                              | —            | —                                          |
| [`webauthn_get`](#webauthn_get)       | Both            | `webauthn_response`      | `invalid_credentials`                                                                                                         | `pop`, `mfa` | `identifier`                               |
| [`webauthn_create`](#webauthn_create) | Both            | `webauthn_response`      | `invalid_credentials`                                                                                                         | —            | `identifier`, `user`, `excludeCredentials` |
| [`totp`](#totp)                       | Both            | `otp`                    | `invalid_credentials`                                                                                                         | `otp`        | `identifier`                               |
| [`recovery_code`](#recovery_code)     | Interaction API | `recovery_code`          | `invalid_credentials`                                                                                                         | —            | `identifier`                               |
| [`recovery_codes`](#recovery_codes)   | Interaction API | `acknowledged`           | —                                                                                                                             | —            | `codes`                                    |
| [`totp_setup`](#totp_setup)           | Interaction API | `otp`                    | `invalid_credentials`                                                                                                         | —            | `identifier`, `secret`, `otpauth_uri`      |
| [`consent`](#consent)                 | Interaction API | `decision`, `remember`   | —                                                                                                                             | —            | `identifier`                               |
| [`select_account`](#select_account)   | Interaction API | `account`                | `account_unavailable`                                                                                                         | —            | `accounts`                                 |
| [`upstream`](#upstream)               | Interaction API | `provider`               | `provider_unavailable`, `provider_declined`, `provider_error`, `unknown_identity`, `too_many_requests`, `service_unavailable` | —            | —                                          |
| [`upstream_link`](#upstream_link)     | Interaction API | `decision`               | `already_linked`, `provider_linked`, `account_unavailable`                                                                    | —            | —                                          |
| [`register`](#register)               | Interaction API | —                        | —                                                                                                                             | —            | —                                          |
| [`sign_in`](#sign_in)                 | Interaction API | —                        | —                                                                                                                             | —            | —                                          |
| [`device_code`](#device_code)         | Interaction API | `user_code`              | `invalid_user_code`                                                                                                           | —            | —                                          |
| [`device_confirm`](#device_confirm)   | Interaction API | `decision`               | —                                                                                                                             | —            | `location`, `network`, `user_agent`        |
| [`logout_confirm`](#logout_confirm)   | Interaction API | `decision`               | —                                                                                                                             | —            | `accounts`                                 |

"Both" means the Interaction API and the FiPA endpoint. Where a step only the Interaction API serves would come next, the FiPA endpoint answers `redirect_to_web`.

### identifier

`urn:qauth:ia:identifier:v1-rc.0` — Asks who is signing in.

Identifier-first sign-in (ADR-020 §3). Every identifier, known or unknown, gets the same next step, so the screen reveals nothing about which accounts exist (ADR-017 Decision 4). Offered as an alternative of a later step, it is the account switch: answering it ends the interaction and starts a new one for the same authorization request, and the result is a redirect to the ceremony app’s page of the new interaction. Nothing proved for the first account carries over (#592). Beside `select_account` it is "Use another account", which ends no session: it adds an account, and the accounts the chooser lists stay signed in (ADR-019 Decision 3). Beside any other step it is "Not you?", which also signs the browser out of the account the screen shows, and of no other account, so that the next person or the next app on a shared device does not continue as that account; its label says that it signs out (#964). The account shown is the one a sign-in during the interaction proved, the signed-in user a consent is for or, while nobody has signed in during the interaction, the account the identifier the person gave names. Its sessions that end: the one a sign-in during the interaction started (#896); the session the browser was already signed in with when the interaction started, such as for a consent or a sign-in the app asked for again, when it is that account’s (#964); and, when the server can check the browser’s session cookie, the session it names if that belongs to the same account (a sign-in again in another tab). The cookie is cleared when it names one of them. A session of another account stays.

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/identifier.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/identifier.json)

### password

`urn:qauth:ia:password:v1-rc.0` — Asks for the password.

The password factor. A rejected password, an unknown account and a disabled account give the same `invalid_credentials`, after the same timing floor (ADR-017 Decisions 3 and 4). Works without JavaScript: the form posts straight to the auth server with the step’s CSRF value (ADR-019 Decision 5).

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/password.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/password.json)

### email_code

`urn:qauth:ia:email_code:v1-rc.0` — Asks for the code mailed to the account’s address.

An emailed code proves control of a mailbox: it verifies a password account and recovers an account. It is never a sign-in factor and adds no `amr` value (ADR-017 Decision 5). For `recovery`, an address that gets no mail (no account, or no password) gets a phantom code: the step comes with the same `expires_in` and `resend_after`, and its answers are refused with the same errors at the same times as a real code’s (`invalid_credentials` for a wrong code, `code_expired` once `expires_in` has passed), so neither error tells a known address from an unknown one. An answer with no `otp` asks for the code again. Works without JavaScript.

- Params: `purpose`, `length`, `expires_in`, `resend_after`
- Schema: [steps/email_code.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/email_code.json)

### new_password

`urn:qauth:ia:new_password:v1-rc.0` — Asks for a new password.

Sets a password through the one password policy (ADR-017 Decision 8): at registration, at the end of a reset, or when an admin or a breach-list match requires a new one (ADR-020 §3). The reasons of a refusal are returned, never prose. The page marks the field for password managers, with the identifier from the personal data as the username. Works without JavaScript.

- Params: `purpose`, `min_length`, `max_length`, `reasons`
- Schema: [steps/new_password.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/new_password.json)

### password_reset

`urn:qauth:ia:password_reset:v1-rc.0` — Starts a password reset.

A path marker: answering it starts a reset. The next step is `email_code` with `purpose` `recovery` for every address, known or not; mail goes only to a known address with a password. An unknown address gets a phantom code, with the same `expires_in` and `resend_after` and the same error sequence as a real one, so the reset says nothing about whether the address has an account. A reset never unlocks an account whose strongest authenticator is stronger than email (ADR-017 Decision 8).

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/password_reset.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/password_reset.json)

### captcha

`urn:qauth:ia:captcha:v1-rc.0` — Asks for a bot challenge answer.

A bot challenge, when a soft threshold requires one; the pending step resumes after it (ADR-017 Decisions 4 and 7). By default the built-in proof of work, whose script the ceremony app serves from the realm origin. An operator may name a hosted provider for the sign-up and sign-in pages only (ADR-019 Decision 5). A required challenge needs JavaScript and is never skipped. The built-in proof of work (`provider` `pow`) is solved as follows. The answer, `captcha_token`, is a nonce: 1 to 16 ASCII digits `0` to `9`, with no sign and no leading zero (`0` itself is a nonce). The engine takes the SHA-256 digest of the UTF-8 bytes of the challenge, a colon and the nonce, `<challenge>:<nonce>`, with the challenge as the text it is, not base64url-decoded. It accepts the nonce when that digest starts with at least `difficulty` zero bits, read from the most significant bit of its first byte. Any such nonce passes; trying 0, 1, 2 and so on finds one after about 2^`difficulty` hashes. A puzzle takes one answer: a wrong nonce gets the step back with `captcha_failed` and a new challenge. A token the answer’s schema refuses is an invalid answer: it is not checked, and the challenge stays. QAuth’s shared test vectors, `test-vectors/interaction/proof-of-work.json` in its repository, hold cases to check a solver against.

- Params: `provider`, `challenge`, `difficulty`, or `provider`, `name`, `site_key`
- Schema: [steps/captcha.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/captcha.json)

### webauthn_get

`urn:qauth:ia:webauthn_get:v1-rc.0` — Asks for a passkey.

Passkey sign-in: the WebAuthn Level 3 request options as JSON, for `PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON()`. Discoverable credentials only: the options never carry `allowCredentials`, so the step read reveals no account’s passkeys (ADR-017 Decision 4, ADR-019 Decision 6). The engine checks that the passkey belongs to the transaction’s account. The RP ID is the realm’s host (ADR-019 Decision 2). Needs JavaScript.

- Params: `challenge`, `rpId`, `timeout`, `userVerification`
- Schema: [steps/webauthn_get.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/webauthn_get.json)

### webauthn_create

`urn:qauth:ia:webauthn_create:v1-rc.0` — Offers or asks to create a passkey.

Passkey enrolment. `options` is the WebAuthn Level 3 creation options as JSON without `user` and `excludeCredentials`, which are the account’s own data and come with the personal data; the page joins the two for `PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()`. The RP ID is the realm’s host and locks at the first enrolment (ADR-019 Decision 2). Enrolment adds no `amr` value. Needs JavaScript.

- Params: `optional`, `options`
- Schema: [steps/webauthn_create.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/webauthn_create.json)

### totp

`urn:qauth:ia:totp:v1-rc.0` — Asks for the code of the authenticator app.

A TOTP second factor (RFC 6238) with the fixed parameters of ADR-020 §3: SHA-1, six digits, 30 seconds, one step of tolerance. An accepted code is never accepted twice (ADR-017 Decision 8). Works without JavaScript.

- Params: `digits`
- Schema: [steps/totp.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/totp.json)

### recovery_code

`urn:qauth:ia:recovery_code:v1-rc.0` — Asks for one of the account’s recovery codes.

A recovery code stands in for a second factor after the first, or for the passkey of a passkey-only account. Only the hosted pages redeem one; the FiPA endpoint answers `redirect_to_web` for that path. It adds no `amr` value and never `mfa`, so a policy that needs a second factor makes the person bind a new one before the transaction completes (ADR-017 Decisions 4 and 8). Works without JavaScript.

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/recovery_code.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/recovery_code.json)

### recovery_codes

`urn:qauth:ia:recovery_codes:v1-rc.0` — Shows a new set of recovery codes once.

A new recovery-code set: issued at the first enrolment of a second factor, at the registration of a passkey-only account, and when the person regenerates the set (ADR-017 Decision 8). The codes are personal data: readable with the flow cookie while this step is current, and never after. The answer confirms the person saved them.

- Params: `count`
- Schema: [steps/recovery_codes.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/recovery_codes.json)

### totp_setup

`urn:qauth:ia:totp_setup:v1-rc.0` — Sets up an authenticator app.

TOTP enrolment, with the fixed parameters of ADR-020 §3. The secret is personal data: readable with the flow cookie while this step is current, and never after. It is bound only after a first valid code (ADR-017 Decision 8). A verified account binds its first TOTP after a fresh sign-in, with no code mailed to its address: the account decides, never a channel (Decision 8, amended 2026-11-08). An unclaimed account (a password account not yet verified) binds none. The step adds no `amr` value of its own, but the first valid code that binds the secret stands for the sign-in’s `totp` step: the sign-in it completes proves `otp`, with no second code asked. The page shows the secret as a QR code and as text.

- Params: `algorithm`, `digits`, `period`
- Schema: [steps/totp_setup.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/totp_setup.json)

### consent

`urn:qauth:ia:consent:v1-rc.0` — Asks the person to allow or deny what the client asks for.

The OAuth consent decision (#629). The interaction’s `client` names the client, verified domain first (ADR-019 Decision 6), and an AI agent is named as one in QAuth’s own words (ADR-014 §11). The grant is exactly the scope set shown here, which the interaction holds: the answer cannot add a scope. A dangerous scope and `prompt=consent` always reach this step, and an AI agent never skips it; a first-party client may skip it only through the administrative waiver (ADR-017 Decision 9). Works without JavaScript.

- Params: `scopes`, `resources`, `audience`, `agent`, `remember_default`
- Schema: [steps/consent.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/consent.json)

### select_account

`urn:qauth:ia:select_account:v1-rc.0` — Asks which signed-in account to continue with.

The account chooser for `prompt=select_account`, when the browser holds sessions for several accounts of the realm (ADR-019 Decision 3, ADR-020 §3). The list is personal data. "Use another account" answers the `identifier` step, offered beside this one: that starts a new interaction for the same authorization request, and the result is a redirect to its page (#592). It ends no session: the accounts the list shows stay signed in (#964). Needs JavaScript, to read the list.

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/select_account.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/select_account.json)

### upstream

`urn:qauth:ia:upstream:v1-rc.0` — Offers sign-in through an upstream identity provider.

The person picks one of the realm’s upstream identity providers: generic OpenID Connect, or an AuthMethod plugin. It is offered beside the `identifier` step, before anyone is named, alike for every account (ADR-017 Decision 4); on the sign-in to the account an upstream identity joins (`upstream_link`), the provider being linked is left out (#1080). An answer names one provider of the list; the answer’s result is a redirect to the provider (`result: redirect`, or `303` to it for a form post). The provider sends the browser back to `/upstream/<provider>/callback` on the realm host, which checks the answer against the transaction kept server-side for this interaction and its flow cookie, signs in the account that holds that upstream identity, or, for an identity no account holds, asks at the `upstream_link` step whether it starts a new account or joins an existing one, and continues the interaction (on the sign-in to the account an identity joins, an identity no account holds signs in to nothing and creates nothing): the next step’s ceremony page, or the final redirect. A sign-in through a provider ranks with the password in the downgrade rule, below a passkey (ADR-017 Decision 4), and adds no `amr` value. A provider an operator hides is not listed here and stays reachable through the authorization request’s `qauth_upstream` parameter. When the callback refuses while the interaction is live, it sends the browser back to the ceremony page, nothing goes to the client, and this step is the current one again, with the other ways in as its alternatives, its `error`, the provider in `error_provider` (#1081) and the callback’s own `trace_id` (#1106): `provider_declined`, the person cancelled or refused at the provider (OAuth `access_denied`); `provider_error`, the provider answered another error, or an answer that failed its checks; `provider_unavailable`, the provider cannot be used now, such as one switched off before its answer came back, or, for an answer, one that cannot be started; `unknown_identity`, the identity the person just proved at the provider signs in to no account here; `too_many_requests`, the sign-in was throttled; `service_unavailable`, a store the sign-in needs could not answer. No code says anything about an account the person has not proved, so each is the same for every account (ADR-017 Decision 4): `unknown_identity` stands as well for an identity whose account cannot sign in through it. On the sign-in to the account an upstream identity joins, `unknown_identity` is the answer for an identity no account holds. A callback that finds no interaction left (it expired, it moved on, or the browser is not the one that started it) goes to the realm’s error page instead (the error page, below). Works without JavaScript: each provider is a button of a plain form post.

- Params: `providers`, `error_provider`
- Schema: [steps/upstream.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/upstream.json)

### upstream_link

`urn:qauth:ia:upstream_link:v1-rc.0` — Asks whether an upstream identity QAuth does not know starts a new account or joins an existing one.

Shown once an upstream identity provider proved an identity no account of the realm holds (#670; ADR-020 §3). The person picks a new account with that identity, which is offered only where the realm allows sign-up and the new account can be verified (`create`), or the account they already have, which they then sign in to in this interaction under its MFA policy: the `identifier` step, and every step that account’s sign-in asks for. That sign-in offers the realm’s other upstream providers beside its first step, never the one being linked (#1080): one proves the account only through an identity the account already holds, a passkey the account holds is still asked for after it, and an identity no account holds signs in to nothing and creates nothing. No password reset is offered. The identity joins that account only once that sign-in completes, in the same browser and the same interaction. A link refused when it would be written comes back to this step with its reason as `error`, the reason `user.upstream_link_failed` records (#1081): `already_linked`, another account holds the identity; `provider_linked`, the account signed in to already holds an identity of this provider; `account_unavailable`, that account can no longer take a link. Nothing was linked and nothing went to the client. The step then offers no choice: `create` is `false`, an answer is refused with `invalid_answer`, and the page says why and offers the cancel, which ends the authorization request with `access_denied` (an account page’s link goes back to its page). Where the sign-in to the account had already finished the interaction, the step is the first of a new interaction for the same request, and the answer that finished it leads to that interaction’s ceremony page. Nothing on the step names the identity or the account: no address and no hint, and no account is ever found by an attribute such as an email address. Works without JavaScript: each choice is a button of a plain form post.

- Params: `provider`, `create`
- Schema: [steps/upstream_link.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/upstream_link.json)

### register

`urn:qauth:ia:register:v1-rc.0` — Turns a sign-in into a registration.

A path marker (#1079): answering it turns the sign-in into a registration in the same interaction, for the same authorization request, at the registration’s first round, as `prompt=create` (OpenID Connect Prompt Create 1.0) would have started it (ADR-017 Decision 8): the `captcha` step first where the realm or the client requires one, then the address step (`identifier`), with a passkey to create the account with before it while passkey sign-in is on, and `sign_in` beside it. The request the interaction holds does not change, and the registration ends as one `prompt=create` started: in a code for that request, with no `amr` and no `auth_time`. Offered as an alternative of a sign-in’s first step, before anyone is named, alike for every account (ADR-017 Decision 4), and only while the realm allows sign-up (`accounts.allowSignUp`), the client’s operator-set `hosted_flows` name `register` and the request carries no `max_age` and no `prompt=login`: the rules `prompt=create` meets at the authorization endpoint, but for the `openid` scope, which only `prompt=create` needs. Never offered on a sign-in to join an upstream identity to an account (`upstream_link`) nor on the account page’s sign-in. The rules are read again on every round: an answer to it once they no longer hold is refused with `invalid_answer`, and the sign-in stays where it was. The page shows it as “Create an account”. Works without JavaScript.

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/register.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/register.json)

### sign_in

`urn:qauth:ia:sign_in:v1-rc.0` — Turns a registration back into a sign-in.

A path marker (#1079), the way back from `register`: answering it turns the registration into a sign-in in the same interaction, for the same authorization request, at the sign-in’s first round: the `identifier` step, with a passkey before it while passkey sign-in is on and the realm’s upstream providers beside it. Offered as an alternative of a registration’s address step, before anyone is named and before any mailbox is proved, whether the registration began with `prompt=create` or with `register`. Nothing the registration kept carries over: the sign-in starts empty. After the mailbox is proved, an address an account holds goes on to that account’s sign-in by itself, as before. The page shows it as “I have an account”. Works without JavaScript.

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/sign_in.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/sign_in.json)

### device_code

`urn:qauth:ia:device_code:v1-rc.0` — Asks for the code the device shows.

Code entry for the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (RFC 8628 §3.3). Unknown, expired and used codes give the same `invalid_user_code`. Entry is rate-limited per code, per session and per address. A person who arrives through `verification_uri_complete` skips this step and still confirms on `device_confirm` (ADR-020 §3). Works without JavaScript.

- Params: `length`
- Schema: [steps/device_code.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/device_code.json)

### device_confirm

`urn:qauth:ia:device_confirm:v1-rc.0` — Asks the person to confirm the device in front of them.

The explicit confirmation of a device authorization, always asked, also after `verification_uri_complete` (ADR-020 §3). The screen warns that nobody else should have given the person the code, and shows where the request came from: the requesting device’s approximate location, network and user agent, which are personal data, and its start time. The consent step always follows, even for a client that may skip consent elsewhere. The device details come with the personal data, so this step needs JavaScript: a page shows them before it offers `confirm`.

- Params: `user_code`, `requested_at`
- Schema: [steps/device_confirm.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/device_confirm.json)

### logout_confirm

`urn:qauth:ia:logout_confirm:v1-rc.0` — Asks the person to confirm signing out.

The confirmation of an RP-initiated logout (ADR-019 Decision 4). The interaction’s `client` names the app that asked, when the request identified one. A browser may hold several accounts’ sessions, so the person signs out of this account or of every account on the browser (ADR-019 Decision 3). Works without JavaScript, without the account list.

- Params: —
- Schema: [steps/logout_confirm.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/steps/logout_confirm.json)

## Brand

Every step read carries the realm's `brand`: the theme tier of ADR-019 Decision 5. It holds a logo an admin uploaded (served from the realm origin), light and dark colours, a font from the safe list (`system`, `inter`, `noto_sans`, `atkinson_hyperlegible`, `ibm_plex_sans`, `source_sans_3`), links to the terms, the privacy notice and help, the realm's strings by locale, and whether dark mode is enabled. There are no uploaded templates, CSS or script. A realm that set nothing gets the defaults: `system` and dark mode enabled, and every member left out keeps the ceremony app's own value.

## Errors

An error is an RFC 9457 problem details document (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` and a `trace_id`, as on the other API families ([API conventions](/reference/api-conventions/#errors)). Its `type` and `title` are the code's entry on [Problem types](/reference/problem-types/). It carries no `detail`, `instance` or `errors` list: a page shows its own text for the code, with the trace id. A page treats a code it does not know by its HTTP status.

| Code                     | Status | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bad_request`            | 400    | The request is malformed and no more specific code applies.                                                                                                                                          |
| `invalid_answer`         | 400    | The answer does not match the schema of the step it names, names a step the interaction does not offer, or repeats a field. The engine was not called.                                               |
| `forbidden`              | 403    | The request is not same-origin, or its CSRF value is missing, already used or not the current step’s. The engine was not called.                                                                     |
| `interaction_expired`    | 410    | The interaction is unknown, expired or finished, the flow cookie does not belong to it, or a finish came after the browser session its sign-in started had ended. Every reason gets this one answer. |
| `content_too_large`      | 413    | The request body is larger than the server accepts.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `unsupported_media_type` | 415    | The request body is neither `application/json` nor `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.                                                                                                              |
| `misdirected_request`    | 421    | The server does not answer for the host the request names.                                                                                                                                           |
| `too_many_requests`      | 429    | Too many requests. `Retry-After` says when to try again.                                                                                                                                             |
| `internal_error`         | 500    | The server failed. `trace_id` finds the failure in the server log.                                                                                                                                   |
| `service_unavailable`    | 503    | The server cannot answer now, for example while a store the engine needs is down. It fails closed.                                                                                                   |

## Paths

- The prefix `/interaction/v1-rc.0/wallet/` is reserved for the wallet return leg (ADR-013). No operation of this document is served under it.
- The auth server serves this document at `/interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json`.

## Error page

Some endings leave no interaction for a ceremony page to read: an upstream provider's callback for an interaction that expired, moved on or belongs to another browser, and the pages an RP-initiated logout ends on (#1106). A realm may name its ceremony app's error page for them, in its `ceremonyApp.errorPage` policy. With it set, the auth server answers `303 See Other` to that path with the query below and renders no page; without it, it renders its own page. A refusal that leaves the interaction live goes back to the interaction's ceremony page instead, as its step's `error` with the refusing request's `trace_id`.

| Code                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interaction_expired` | An upstream provider sent the browser back for a sign-in with no interaction left to continue: it expired or ended, it moved on, or the browser is not the one that started it. Nothing was signed in, and nothing went to the client.                                                 |
| `logout_refused`      | An app’s sign-out request was refused: it named a return URI the app did not register, a client that is not the ID token hint’s audience, or a client that may not be used. Nothing was signed out.                                                                                    |
| `logout_finished`     | A sign-out ended with no app the browser is sent back to: `signed_out` says whether this browser now holds no session of the realm, and `host`, when present, names the app the person would go back to, which the browser is not sent to because the operator did not set the app up. |

| Query member | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`       | Always: one of the codes. A page that does not know a code shows a general message.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `trace_id`   | The id the server logged the request that sent the browser here under, as a problem document’s `trace_id` (ADR-019 Decision 7): the page shows it, so an operator can find the request. Absent when that id is not one a `trace_id` can carry. |
| `signed_out` | With `logout_finished`: `true` when this browser holds no session of the realm, `false` when it is still signed in (the person chose to stay).                                                                                                 |
| `host`       | With `logout_finished` and `signed_out=true`, at most: the host of the app’s registered return URI, in ASCII form, for a web app the operator did not set up. Text to show, never a link.                                                      |

- The page is a path of the ceremony app on the realm origin, under `/ui/` as `/ui/interaction/{interactionId}` is. The realm names it in its `ceremonyApp.errorPage` policy; the policy takes nothing but such a path, so the auth server never sends the browser to another origin from it.
- Every member of the query is display data, as anyone can write the same URL. The page trusts nothing navigational from it (ADR-019 Decision 5): it never builds a link or a redirect from `host` or any other member, and it shows each as text. It changes nothing and asks for nothing, so a forged query can only show a wrong message.
- The page reads no interaction: there is none to read, and no step to answer. The person’s way on is their own, such as going back to the app they came from; the realm’s brand `help` link says where to get help.

## Replacement apps

A sign-in UI that replaces the reference ceremony app and follows this contract is a supported setup (#618). Beside the contract, it needs:

- **A typed client.** Generate one from [openapi.json](/interaction/v1-rc.0/openapi.json) with any OpenAPI 3.1 client generator, and generate it again when the path's release candidate changes. QAuth's own client, `libs/shared/interaction-client`, is generated the same way, for the reference ceremony app. It is not published as a package, and neither is its proof-of-work solver: the SDKs QAuth publishes are those of [ADR-018](/reference/records/adr/018-1-0-scope-and-stability/#6-sdks-and-the-rust-core) §6, and what this API promises is its document and its step schemas, not a client library.
- **A solver for the built-in proof of work.** The [`captcha`](#captcha) step states its rule, which is all a solver needs. Check a solver against `test-vectors/interaction/proof-of-work.json`, the shared test vectors QAuth's own check and solver run.
- **A hosted provider's script**, when the operator named a hosted provider for the bot challenge: the provider's own, loaded from the script hosts the operator listed (ADR-019 Decision 5).
